question.text: From a height of 12 m, a ball is projected straight up with an initial speed of 18 m/s. Exactly at this moment, an open-platform lift crosses the 5 m mark while ascending at a steady speed of 2 m/s. Taking g = 9.8 m/s², calculate:

parts.label: a
parts.asks: the time and location where the ball encounters the platform,

parts.label: b
parts.asks: the velocity of the ball measured relative to the platform upon collision.

conditions: ball projected vertically upward from y = 12 m with v₀ = 18 m/s
elevator ascends at constant velocity 2 m/s from y = 5 m at t = 0

solution.approach: Write the ball's height under gravity and the elevator's height at constant speed as functions of time, set them equal to find when they meet, then find their relative velocity.

steps.text: Write the ball's height using free-fall kinematics and the elevator's height using constant velocity.
Set the two heights equal and simplify to a quadratic in t.
Solve the quadratic and keep the positive root.
Find the meeting height using the elevator's equation.
Find the relative velocity of the ball with respect to the elevator at this instant.

final_answer.value: (a) the ball meets the elevator at t ≈ 3.66 s, at a height of about 12.31 m. (b) relative velocity of the ball with respect to the elevator ≈ 19.83 m/s, directed downward.

common_mistakes.text: Solving for when the ball returns to the elevator's starting height of 5 m, ignoring that the elevator itself keeps moving up, which gives the wrong time t ≈ 4.03 s.
Assuming the ball is still moving upward at the meeting instant instead of already falling, giving a wrong relative velocity of about 15.83 m/s instead of 19.83 m/s.
